root.meaning: coffee (earlier perhaps a kind of wine)
root.note: qahwa is certain as the source. Its own origin is disputed: Arab dictionaries say it first meant wine; a link with the Kaffa region in Ethiopia is often told but doubted.

history: Coffee came to England in the early 1600s, and the first London coffee house opened in 1652. The word travelled a long way. In Arabic the drink was qahwa. The Ottoman Turks made it kahve, and from Turkish it went to Italian caffè and Dutch koffie. English probably took it from Dutch, because Dutch traders brought the beans to northern Europe. Where qahwa itself comes from is not certain. Some old Arab dictionaries say it was first a word for wine. Others connect it with Kaffa, a region in Ethiopia where coffee grows wild, but many experts doubt this. The word café, a place to drink coffee, came later from French.
historyEinfach: Coffee is an Arabic word. In Arabic it is qahwa. In Turkish it is kahve. Then the word went to Europe. In Dutch it is koffie, and in English coffee. The first coffee house in London opened in 1652. Café comes from French.

elsewhere.text: The English word starts here. Coffee was drunk in Yemen and Arabia long before Europe knew it, and the Arabic name went west together with the drink.

Turkish kahve was the bridge to Europe. Istanbul's coffee houses (kahvehane) were famous, and Europeans first met coffee there. Turkish kahvaltı, ‘breakfast’, is built on the same word: ‘something before coffee’.
